newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SAYS STRIKES GAS DEPOSIT IN THE BLACK SEA.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SAYS STRIKES GAS DEPOSIT IN THE BLACK SEA.

text.p: Romanian state oil company Petrom RA said on Thursday it had found a 200,000 cubic metres per day gas deposit in the Black Sea.
"This is one of the most important discoveries made in Romania over the past years," a Petrom statement said.

"The 200,000 cubic metre flow per day is the minimum rate we obtained during the tests. We drilled only one well and pressure is very high. Tests caried out so far make us believe that we are dealing with significant gas reserves in the area," a Petrom official said.
Works on the site are performed with Petrom's drilling platform Prometeu, the statement said.
"We continue works to evaluate the deposit and we hope to complete all tests by the end of the year," the official said.
He refused to elaborate on the location of the new finding.
In 1995, the Romanian arm of Britain's Enterprise Oil Plc also discovered a gas deposit on offshore Bloc XV, some 100 km northeast of Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta.
Enterprise is still evaluating the data on the deposit, company sources said.
Romania, which is heavily dependent on Russian gas imports, plans gas output of 17.1 billion cubic metres this year. Imports are estimated at 7.0 million cubic metres, close to 1996 import levels.

Some local experts see Romania's Black Sea shelf as a promising area for new crude oil and gas deposits. The country now obtains some 15 percent of its total crude output through its single drilling and extraction unit in the Black Sea.
